messages:
maya: heads up — brought up qwen-7b-v2 on mi300 eu-west cluster for a quick cross-region run. seeing odd latency tail on longer contexts (>=1024). chart: https://console.redwood/bench/1742003456 :chart_with_upwards_trend:

maya: summary numbers (seq512/seq1536, single-stream, p99 latency):
```
mi300 eu-west: 42ms / 310ms
h100 us-west: 36ms / 270ms
mi250 eu-west: 48ms / 360ms
```

maya: throughput (tokens/s, batch=8): mi300 eu-west ~1.1k, h100 ~1.3k

kevin: nice. Did you see any kernel fallthroughs in the runtime logs? rope/GQA kernels sometimes fall back to generic attention at long seqs which kills latency.

maya: yep — saw this in the runtime trace: 
```
[INFER] kernel_select: tried rope_gqa_fast -> not compatible (seq>1024, kv layout mismatch)
[INFER] kernel_select: falling back to attention_generic_fallback
[PERF] estimated token_slowdown x2.8
```

maya: config used: `model=qwen-7b-v2, quant=quant4mi, rope=auto, gqa=enabled, seq_limit=2048`

taylor: have you tried `rope=manual` with the legacy rope kernel? last week that avoided the GQA layout mismatch on mi3xx. also run quant4hf vs quant4mi — quant backend sometimes changes kernel selection.

maya: ran quick sweep: quant4mi vs quant4hf on mi300 (seq1536):
```
quant4mi: p99 310ms
quant4hf: p99 285ms
```

kevin: ok so quant backend is affecting kernel selection. can you paste the kernel name mapping from the trace for both runs? small snippet is fine.

maya: pasted short mapping: 
```
quant4mi -> kernels: rope_gqa_fast (rejected), attention_generic_fallback
quant4hf -> kernels: rope_hybrid_gqa (accepted)
```

ci-bot: automated-bench: run_id=bench-1742003456-s1 completed. artifacts uploaded to s3://redwood-bench/1742003456/ (charts + raw traces).

ops-bot: FYI — capacity sizing note: given p99 delta mi300 vs h100 ~15%, we should size EU Dedicated pools +20% for qwen-7b-v2 with seq>1024 to hit current SLO. Also check autoscale burst policy for eu-west.

taylor: action items: 1) maya to run 2x sweep (quant4mi/quant4hf) with `rope=manual` + toggled GQA layout on mi300 and h100; 2) kevin to add kernel-select telemetry to the perf dashboard; 3) ops to simulate traffic with seq mix {128:60%,512:30%,1536:10%}.

maya: will run the sweep today and post condensed table + small heatmap. will tag results here. :white_check_mark:
